headline: Real Dough reached 9,979 units in week 39, up 31% week over week, while Celeste's exit and air-fryer-led frozen demand sharpen the case for disciplined SKUs, preparation clarity and retailer-level follow-through.

items: Real Dough sold 9,979 units in week 39 (2026-09-20 through 2026-09-26), up 31% from 7,591 in week 38 and 22% above the eight-week average; selling stores rose from 503 to 521.
Week 39 velocity reached 4.31 units per store per week, up 20% from 3.60 in week 38 and 7% above the 13-week average of 4.02.
Festival Foods led the four-week account gains at 3,661 units, up 165% from the prior four weeks; Dierberg's rose 43% and Cub Foods rose 38%.
Oleson's Foods entered with 48 units across two stores, and six new-store records were present in the current sales pulse.

The sales pulse flags 126 quiet stores. The largest groups are Piggly Wiggly (20), Hy-Vee (17), Schnucks (15) and unlisted independents (15); these are source-defined quiet-store records, not confirmed delistings.
Four-week units fell 77% at Kroger Michigan, 59% at Super One and 48% at Kroger Mariano's versus the prior four weeks; Coborns Marketplace fell 95% on a small base of 264 to 14 units.
Conagra is exiting Celeste frozen pizza as part of a SKU-complexity review, signaling that buyer and manufacturer tolerance for low-scale assortment is tightening.

Air fryers are in 71% of American homes and more than half of owners report buying more frozen food because of the appliance, yet only 33% of shoppers say most products they buy include air-fryer directions, according to NFRA.
Review week 39 drivers with Festival Foods, Dierberg's and Cub Foods, then isolate whether distribution, promotion or repeat velocity explains the gains before using them in buyer materials.

Prioritize store-level follow-up on the 126 quiet stores, starting with Piggly Wiggly, Hy-Vee, Schnucks and the Kroger divisions showing four-week declines; confirm distribution and inventory before treating the records as demand weakness.

Run formal cook-quality and food-safety testing for air-fryer preparation; if validated, add clear instructions to packaging and retailer product pages rather than making an unsupported convenience claim.
Keep the buyer story disciplined around distinct consumer job, repeatable velocity, margin contribution and a tight five-SKU architecture; Celeste's exit makes assortment productivity more salient.

agency_brief.what_worked: The defensible business proof this week is sales momentum: week 39 units, velocity and selling-store count all improved, with especially strong four-week movement at Festival Foods, Dierberg's and Cub Foods.
agency_brief.what_didnt: No current paid, social or content-performance feed is available, so no creative format, campaign or channel can be called a winner. At retail, Kroger Michigan, Super One, Kroger Mariano's and Coborns Marketplace require diagnosis before more spend or broad success claims.
agency_brief.recommendation: Build near-term messaging around validated preparation ease, premium sourdough quality and specific meal occasions. Treat air-fryer language as a testable product claim, and support buyer-facing creative with the actual week 39 sales proof rather than generic premium language.
agency_brief.competitive_context: Conagra's Celeste exit raises the bar for SKU productivity; New York Bakery is entering frozen snacks with air-fryer-ready, protein-positioned products; frozen handhelds are growing while total frozen dinners and entrees soften; and Sargento's completed La Terra Fina acquisition shows a Wisconsin CPG peer building a dedicated route into grocery and club deli departments.
